title: Being an ambassador of goodwill and friendly audiences
summary: He explains the goodwill tours as coming from musicians' appreciation of fans, recalls leaders smiling on the job, and says true friends tell him when he misses notes.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Louis Armstrong, a wonderful guy. He's been traveling all over the world as ambassador of goodwill for the United States of America. We'll hear more about that after this message.
A great new marble cake mix from Betty Crocker.

The star is Mr. Louis Armstrong. And recently, Louis traveled 60,000 miles in 45 days on behalf of the United States of America. Quite a record. Quite a guy. Louis, how did you happen to start in this field of yours being an ambassador of goodwill?

Well, I mean, we always loved each other and music in New Orleans. It comes from musicians appreciating each other. No matter where you meet him, what you say, man. Yeah. And your wife. Yeah. And your fans. A lot of them don't play music, but they know just what you're doing. And appreciation. That's why you can always sit in the crowd. And they all try to get backstage. Autographs. And I put in there, catch everybody, because I light them up and things like that.
And if you smile and are friendly to them, perhaps they get a better impression of the people in the United States. Yeah.

In the early days, I used to notice my leaders. They come on the job with a nice smile. They're going to have good music that night. Yeah. You know, everybody wake up, you know. Any of your friends ever criticize you for doing this? Well, no. They don't criticize me for doing that. But if I miss one of them notes, they don't fail to tell me. I mean, some of your friends criticize you for... Well, I call them my friends when they tell me the truth. Yeah. Yeah. They're friends.
